model: Claude Code (skill) — builds with HTML/Canvas/Three.js/GSAP/Remotion, renders to MP4
title: video-director: A Claude skill for directing, building and verifying code-rendered videos
prompt_text:
Your AI promo videos look cheap because nobody checks them before posting. This free Claude Code skill makes Claude plan, build, render and then QA its own video before you ever see it. github.com/win4r/video-director

What it does:
- You ask in plain words, like "Make a 15 second looping launch video for our CLI"
- It plans the film in numbers first, and check_timeline.py validates the plan before any code is written
- It builds the video as code (HTML, Canvas, Three.js, GSAP or Remotion), rendered frame by frame to MP4
- qa_video.py then measures the render: hook text size and contrast, black first frame, flashes, freezes, loudness, silences
- Hook and call to action land on screen by 3 seconds, readable with sound off

In the author's small test, runs with the skill passed 28/28 checks vs 25/28 without it. They say treat it as a direction, not proof.

Install:
  git clone github.com/win4r/video-director
  cp -R video-director/video-director ~/.claude/skills/

Needs ffmpeg, Python 3 with numpy and Pillow, and Node with Playwright. MIT licence.

Money angle: SaaS founders and local brands need a short launch or promo video every time they ship something. Sell it as a fixed-price video, and let the QA step catch mistakes before the client does.

What would you make first with it, a launch video or an explainer?
